SUBAWARD vs. SUBCONTRACT

KEY ASPECT
SUBAWARD
(Subrecipient)
SUBCONTRACT
(Contractor / Vendor)

ROLE IN PROJECT
Performs a portion of the sponsored
project's scope of work.
Provides goods or services that support
the project but do not take part in the
programmatic work.

PROGRAMMATIC
INVOLVEMENT
Exercises programmatic decision-making
and discretion.
Does not exercise programmatic
decision-making; follows directions
provided by MSU.

INTELLECTUAL
CONTRIBUTION
Makes intellectually significant contributions
to the project.
Performs routine or standardized tasks
within its normal business operations.

COMPLIANCE
RESPONSIBILITY
Responsible for compliance with federal
regulations and sponsor requirements
applicable to the award.
Not responsible for compliance with federal
programmatic requirements of the award.

PUBLICATION &
AUTHORSHIP
May publish or co-author results related
to the work.
Does not have rights to publish or claim
authorship related to the project.

BUDGET & SCOPE
DEVELOPMENT
Typically provides its own budget and
statement of work.
Works from a statement of work provided
by MSU; budget developed by MSU.

RELATIONSHIP
TYPE
Federal assistance relationship;
subject to Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200).
Procurement relationship governed by
federal and institutional procurement rules.

MONITORING
APPROACH
Requires ongoing monitoring and oversight
by MSU.
Requires oversight to ensure contractor
performance and deliverables.

MORGAN
STATE UNIVERSITY
★
Correct classification is critical. Misclassifying a subaward as a subcontract (or vice versa)
can result in compliance issues, audit findings, and potential financial consequences.
